front.title: A DNS Resource Record for PRP References

abstract.t: This document specifies the PRP DNS resource record, which associates a DNS owner name with one or more typed PRP references. Each RDATA contains exactly one IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST, or GROUPCAST reference rather than an IP address, host locator, service priority, public key, or authority proof.
The record is optional integration. PRP operation does not depend on DNS, and DNS publication does not replace the class-specific authentication or authorization required to use a reference.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An operator can need to publish a PRP identity, discovery alias, logical multicast, or governed groupcast for a DNS name without publishing a machine address. This document defines a data RRTYPE whose RDATA is exactly one canonical PRP reference.

The association is directional: a DNS owner name names references selected by the publisher. DNS publication does not prove possession, membership, control, administration, participation, or application authorization, and does not make the DNS server or hosting machine the referenced peer.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Scope
section.t: The proposed mnemonic is PRP. The numeric RRTYPE is assigned by IANA. It is an ordinary data RR and defines no new DNS class, opcode, label, reverse tree, underscored name, or additional-section processing.

This profile accepts the four defined PRP reference classes: IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST, and GROUPCAST. Content references, machine locators, authority proofs, representative keys, genesis records, administration events, and application parameters are outside the RDATA format.

This document specifies the DNS carrier, not how identifiers are formed or how authority over a referenced object is established. Those semantics belong to the applicable PRP class and suite specifications. They can evolve without changing this RRTYPE while the reference envelope, class code, suite number, and suite-defined identifier length remain unchanged.

section.name: RDATA Wire Format
section.t: The RDATA is exactly one canonical binary PRP reference:

Bits 1 through 0 of reference_header encode the reference class and bits 7 through 2 are reserved and zero. Header values 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, and 0x03 designate IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST, and GROUPCAST respectively; all other values have nonzero reserved bits and MUST be rejected. RDLENGTH equals 35 or 51 for the closed initial suite set. A consumer MUST reject an unassigned suite or a length that is not exact for that suite. No compression pointer or DNS name occurs in RDATA. Canonical DNSSEC processing leaves these octets unchanged.

All four classes denote PRP Self-Certifying Identifier References (SCIRs), as described in . Each class has distinct certifying material and validation rules and does not inherit IDENTITY possession semantics. For DNS processing, every identifier is an opaque octet string of the exact suite-defined length. DNS storage supplies no class-specific authority.

The suite number and class both participate in reference equality. Equal lengths do not make classes or suites interchangeable. An unknown suite is unsupported by a PRP-aware consumer and length alone MUST NOT select one. This document does not create a DNS subregistry for PRP classes or suites.
Authoritative servers and resolvers that do not understand the assigned type can store and forward it under the unknown-RR rules in .

section.name: Presentation Format
section.t: The type-specific presentation consists of three whitespace-separated tokens:

reference-class is one of the decimal integers 0, 1, 2, or 3 and reference-suite is an unsigned decimal integer from 1 through 65535, without a sign or leading zero. identifier-hex contains exactly two hexadecimal digits per identifier octet, without a prefix or separator. Input hexadecimal is case-insensitive; canonical output uses lowercase. The suite determines the required number of digits.
For implementations without type-specific support, the generic presentation in remains valid. It is not a second PRP-specific encoding.

section.name: RRset Semantics
section.t: A PRP RRset MAY contain multiple distinct references. Identical duplicate RDATA values do not add another reference. RRset order MUST NOT express priority, preference, fallback, or rotation. An application selects supported references of its requested class under its own policy. Failure to authenticate or authorize one reference MUST NOT silently downgrade to another class or weaker suite.

Adding or removing a DNS reference does not prove migration, delegation, equivalence, or an ordered transition. A still-valid cached RRset can remain usable until its DNS validity expires. DNS replacement, deletion, or TTL expiry MUST NOT by itself terminate or re-identify an established identity, multicast, groupcast, relationship, or session.
CNAME, DNAME, wildcard synthesis, delegation, truncation, TCP retry, negative caching, and ordinary TTL behavior retain their existing DNS semantics. This document defines no special server behavior.

A PRP-aware consumer MUST validate every RDATA in the complete RRset before selecting a reference. A malformed known-suite RDATA fails the association lookup; it MUST NOT be silently omitted to construct a different partial RRset.

section.name: Consumer Validation
section.t: When DNS is the authority for the name-to-reference association, the consumer MUST obtain a Secure DNSSEC validation result and a trusted validation path as specified by and . Bogus or Indeterminate results fail. Insecure DNS is not an authenticated reference binding.

An independently trusted reference or identity pin can instead restrict DNS output to untrusted discovery hints. DNS MUST NOT replace, broaden, or update such a pin without the pin's separately authorized update mechanism.

DNSSEC authenticates the publisher's DNS assertion; it does not prove civil identity, possession, membership, control, administration, participation, application authorization, or that an answer is the newest publication. After selection, the consumer MUST apply the authority and validation rules of the selected PRP class and suite. Those rules are deliberately outside this DNS carrier specification.
An implementation without admitted semantics for a class MUST treat that reference as unsupported rather than coerce it to another class or infer authority from DNS publication.

section.name: Operational Considerations
section.t: Operators should publish only references intentionally made discoverable. Stable references and query names permit correlation. GROUPCAST and MULTICAST names can expose social structure or communication purpose. DNSSEC does not provide query confidentiality. Operators should select TTLs and signing-validity periods consistent with replacement policy.

Serve-stale behavior can extend availability of old data but does not establish that a reference remains authorized for new operations. A relying application requiring freshness must define and enforce its own acceptable DNS evidence horizon. See .

ul.li: Unsigned or insecure DNS can substitute an attacker reference.
A DNSSEC-valid response can still be stale within applicable DNS and signature-validity rules.
Class-specific authority proof does not prove the DNS-name association; applications requiring both must validate both.
Multiple references have no DNS order or preference; applications must select by requested class and explicit policy.
DNS changes do not revoke established identity, multicast, groupcast, relationship, or session authority and do not override independent pins.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to allocate a new data RRTYPE from the Expert Review range of the DNS Parameters registry, with mnemonic PRP and reference to this document, following .
The application requests no DNS class, opcode, EDNS option, algorithm number, or subsidiary IANA registry.

section.name: RRTYPE Application Summary
section.t: The public submitter is Gustavo Junior Alves, GJ LABS, gjalves@gjalves.com.br. The request is a new data RRTYPE associating a DNS name with one or more typed PRP references. The preferred mnemonic is PRP and no numeric value is requested. The format is compatible with unknown-type handling under RFC 3597. TXT, URI, HIP, A, and AAAA do not supply the same typed binary reference association without adding different semantics.
